sources.title: AASB 9 Financial Instruments
sources.fact: AASB 9 para 5.5.1 requires an expected credit loss allowance for contract assets. Paras 5.5.15 to 5.5.16 prescribe the simplified lifetime expected credit loss approach for trade receivables and contract assets without a significant financing component, including when the AASB 15 para 63 expedient applies. For those with a significant financing component, and for lease receivables, the simplified approach depends on an accounting policy election. Include contract assets in the impairment assessment and confirm the applicable approach before using a provision matrix. The compilation read (AASB9_12-14_COMPdec22_01-23, issued 15 December 2022) states it is operative for reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2023 but before 1 January 2026. No loss amount or provisioning conclusion is adopted from this record.
sources.limitations: Located and read on 25 September 2026 by an agent on the maintainer's instruction. For reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2026, confirm the compilation amended by AASB 2024-2 at standards.aasb.gov.au before relying on paragraph numbers.

sources.title: AASB 137 Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets
sources.fact: AASB 137 governs onerous contracts. Para 66 requires a provision when a contract is onerous. Para 68 defines that condition by comparing unavoidable costs with expected economic benefits, and measures unavoidable costs as the lower of fulfilment costs and compensation or penalties for failure to fulfil. Para 68A includes incremental costs and an allocation of other directly related costs, such as depreciation of plant used on the contract. Para 69 requires recognition of impairment losses on assets used to fulfil the contract before a separate provision is established. The compilation read (AASB137_08-15_COMPdec22_01-23, issued 15 December 2022) states it is operative for reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2023 that end before 28 February 2026. No onerous conclusion or measurement is adopted from this record.
sources.limitations: Located and read on 25 September 2026 by an agent on the maintainer's instruction. The compilation read ends its window at periods ending before 28 February 2026. Confirm the operative compilation at standards.aasb.gov.au for later periods.

sources.title: AASB 1060 General Purpose Financial Statements – Simplified Disclosures for For-Profit and Not-for-Profit Tier 2 Entities
sources.fact: The Tier 2 disclosure set the schedule feeds is in AASB 1060. Para 157 covers general revenue disclosures. Para 158 requires the methods used to recognise revenue for performance obligations satisfied over time and how those methods are applied. Para 159 requires closing contract asset and liability balances if not otherwise separately presented or disclosed. Para 44 covers subclassifications presented in the statement of financial position or the notes. The compilation read (AASB1060_03-20_COMPmar21_07-21, issued 29 March 2021) states it is operative for reporting periods beginning on or after 1 July 2021 but before 1 January 2022. No disclosure conclusion is adopted from this record.
sources.limitations: Located and read on 25 September 2026 by an agent on the maintainer's instruction. The operative window on the page read is narrow and the AASB portal serves later compiled text of AASB 1060. Amending pronouncements AASB 2025-2 and AASB 2025-3 apply to periods beginning on or after 1 January 2026. Confirm the compilation operative for the reporting period at standards.aasb.gov.au before citing paragraph numbers.

sources.title: AASB 1053 Application of Tiers of Australian Accounting Standards
sources.fact: AASB 1053 paras 7 to 9 set the two reporting tiers. Tier 2 uses the recognition and measurement requirements of Tier 1 with substantially reduced disclosures. Paras 11 and 13 govern which entities apply each tier. The workflow sends the tier and framework decision to the engagement lead. The compilation read (AASB1053_06-10_COMPmay22_07-21, issued 2 May 2022) states it is operative for reporting periods beginning on or after 1 July 2021 but before 1 January 2027 that end on or after 30 June 2022. No tier or framework conclusion is adopted from this record.
sources.limitations: Located and read on 25 September 2026 by an agent on the maintainer's instruction. Confirm the operative compilation and any later amending pronouncement at standards.aasb.gov.au at use time.

sources.title: AASB 108 Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting Estimates and Errors
sources.fact: AASB 108 paras 34 to 38 address changes in accounting estimates, including the change in a measure of progress identified in AASB 15 para 43. Para 36 recognises the effect prospectively in profit or loss for the current period, or the current and future periods, as applicable. Para 37 instead adjusts the carrying amount of the related asset, liability or equity item when the change affects those items. The compilation read (AASB108_08-15_COMPmar21_01-23, issued 30 March 2021) states it is operative for reporting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2023 but before 1 January 2027. No change-in-estimate treatment is adopted from this record.

sources.title: ASIC Are you a large or small proprietary company
sources.fact: ASIC's section 'Definition of a large proprietary company - financial years commencing on or after 1 July 2019' sets the size criteria. For those years, a proprietary company is large if it meets at least two of consolidated revenue of $50 million or more, consolidated gross assets of $25 million or more at year end, and 100 or more employees at year end. Each criterion includes the company and its controlled entities. That section also requires large proprietary companies to prepare and lodge annual financial and directors' reports, with the financial report audited unless ASIC grants relief. No size or reporting conclusion is adopted from this record.
sources.limitations: Located and read on 25 September 2026 by an agent on the maintainer's instruction. Thresholds are period-specific. Read the cited section for the relevant financial year before concluding size.

sources.title: ASIC Information Sheet 31 Lodgement of financial reports
sources.fact: ASIC Information Sheet 31, under 'What entities must lodge financial reports?' and 'What documents must be lodged', identifies the reporting entities under s 292 of the Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) and the required documents. The page states it was updated in April 2026. No lodgement obligation conclusion is adopted from this record.

sources.title: ATO Taxation Ruling TR 2018/3 Income tax: tax treatment of long term construction contracts
sources.fact: TR 2018/3 para 2 defines long term construction contracts as contracts whose work extends beyond one income year, including contracts shorter than twelve months that cross income years. Paras 5 to 6 describe the basic and estimated profits approaches and require consistent use across the contract years and similar contracts. Under the basic approach, paras 7 to 9 include amounts billed or billable for work carried out and certified for payment, as well as amounts received. Para 44 applies the ruling to years before and after 7 March 2018, subject to its settlement exception. The ruling was published on 7 March 2018 and identifies its PDF as the authorised version. No tax treatment is adopted from this record.
sources.limitations: Located and read on 25 September 2026 by an agent on the maintainer's instruction. The PDF at https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/pdf/pbr/tr2018-003.pdf is the authorised version. PCG 2026/D2 remains a draft compliance guideline about Part IVA and property development arrangements involving long-term construction contracts. Its para 13 proposes application before and after its issue date when finalised. Check its status at https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?DocID=DPC/PCG2026D2/NAT/ATO/00001 before use and do not treat the draft as a final position.

sources.title: Building and Construction Industry Security of Payment Regulation 2020 (NSW)
sources.fact: The NSW retention money trust requirements are in Part 2. Clause 6 limits application to head contractors whose main contract is valued at $20 million or more, including variations. If the threshold is reached through a later variation, cl 6(4) applies only to subcontracts entered into after that point. For head contractors to whom Part 2 applies, cl 8 requires retention money to be held in trust for the entitled subcontractor and paid to a retention money trust account with an approved ADI as soon as possible and within 5 business days of being required to retain it. The version read is in force from 1 March 2021. No retention classification is adopted from this record.

sources.title: Building and Construction Industry Security of Payment Act 1999 (NSW)
sources.fact: The Security of Payment Act supplies part of the legal context for the AASB 15 para B12 entitlement analysis. It governs payment claims and adjudication for construction work in NSW, and s 12A enables the retention money trust requirements imposed by the Regulation. The version read is in force from 20 August 2024. No entitlement or enforceability conclusion is adopted from this record.
